prs.title: [css-inline-3][editorial] Fix stale text left over from #5329
prs.author: shivamidow
prs.body:
Issue #5329 made an initial letter whose size is less than its sink use over (top) alignment instead of under alignment. Some text was not updated to match:

* The Changes entry for #5329 said "under alignment point", but the resolution and the Block-axis Positioning rules say "over".
* The alt text of the 'initial-letter: 2.51 3' example image said the letter "only aligns at base", but the example text and the image show that only the top aligns.
* The note after the Block-axis Positioning rules described only the under alignment case. It now also covers the size < sink case.

prs.title: [css-overflow-5] Explicitly define that scroll-axis-lock propagates from root to viewport. #13207
prs.author: fred-wang
prs.body:
The wording in this PR is based on similar statements in https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scrollbars/#scrollbar-width

WPT tests:
- https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-overflow/scroll-axis-lock-none-touch-viewport.html
- https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-overflow/scroll-axis-lock-none-wheel-viewport.html
- https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-overflow/scroll-axis-lock-none-touch-subframe.html
- https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-overflow/scroll-axis-lock-none-wheel-subframe.html
- https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-overflow/scroll-axis-lock-not-propagated-from-body-quirks.html

This spec change aligns with what @flackr commented at https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13207#issuecomment-5605720322

`scroll-axis-lock` is currently only supported by Chromium and I landed a [patch to align Chromium's behavior with this change](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8412027).

prs.title: [css-align-3][css-grid-3] Define flow-start/end alignment aliases (#14052)
prs.author: celestepan
prs.body:
Adds specification text for the [CSSWG resolution on flow-start/flow-end](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14052#issuecomment-5193187791).

Defines `flow-start` and `flow-end` as value aliases of `flex-start` and `flex-end`, respectively, and adds them to `<self-position>` and `<content-position>`.

In Grid Lanes, both spellings follow the container's item-placement direction in the aligned axis, including reversal. Without reversal in that axis, they behave as logical `start` and `end`. The existing Flexbox behavior is preserved.

Updates the corresponding Grid Lanes alignment text and removes statements that incorrectly limit placement-relative alignment to Flexbox.  Updates the Flexbox text to use `flow-start` and `flow-end` as the canonical values.

Specifies `flow-start`/`flow-end` as the canonical serialized spellings, with an issue retaining the resolution's web-compatibility caveat.

References #14052.

prs.title: [mediaqueries-5] Let browser match when the browser display mode is in use #14125
prs.author: marcoscaceres
prs.body: A page whose manifest has no `display` member is an application context whose applied display mode is `browser`, so `browser` has to match there. This fixes the sentence from [the application display-mode change](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/pull/14587) that limited `browser` to non-application contexts.
